title: The Burning Hollow
premise: Ansel Lockridge, a memory-thief and ledger-keeper for the Hollow Guild, has spent years making themselves forgettable—until the border wards collapse the same night the stars vanish, and every stolen memory in the guild's vault begins to bleed back into their owners. Hunting the source, Ansel discovers the wards were fed by a king's memories, devoured over decades by the thing wearing his crown: a hollow-born parasite that eats belonging itself. To unbind the king, Ansel must surrender the one memory they swore never to trade—the found family that made them whole—and lead the guild's misfit thieves into the palace on the longest night. In the end Ansel gives up their past to free the king, but the family they built refuses to let that sacrifice stand, stitching a new memory of Ansel from everything they shared, proving that belonging is not something remembered but something remade.
about_author: L. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we keep and the things we lose. They write fantasy about outsiders building families in the cracks of broken worlds.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On the night of the autumn market, Ansel records the guild's latest trades—a bottled first kiss, a soldier's cowardice—and steals a sliver of memory to pay their own rent. The beat establishes Ansel's careful invisibility and the quiet ache beneath their competence.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Scars
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Guildmaster Vess sends Ansel to inspect the border wardstones, which hum wrong, like a struck bell going silent. Ansel meets Wren, a runaway hedge-witch who can hear the wards screaming. The beat is unease: the world's oldest protections are dying.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, anchored to Ansel. Every star gutters out at once; the wards fall like cut strings; and the guild's memory-vault ruptures, sending stolen memories flying home to their owners. Panic erupts as clients arrive demanding returns. The beat is chaos shattering Ansel's controlled life.

chapters.title: What Came Home
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A returned memory nearly kills a client, and Ansel realizes the vault's contents are being pulled by something vast and hungry. Vess orders the guild to go dark, but Ansel keeps one ledger page: a royal seal from forty years ago. The beat is dread mixed with stubborn curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Heard Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, newly sheltering with the guild, describes the silence where the stars should sing—an old hedge-song her grandmother taught her. She recognizes the hunger in it. The beat is tentative connection; Wren and Ansel begin an unlikely partnership.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Forgetting
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. To buy passage toward the capital, Ansel trades a memory to a river-ferryman and feels the hole it leaves. Flashback reveals Ansel was sold to the guild as a child and chose forgetting as armor. The beat is grief surfacing through pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Ansel and Wren's POV, alternating. In the capital, the king appears at a festival—but his smile doesn't reach his eyes, and no one remembers his face afterward. Courtiers move like sleepwalkers. The beat is creeping horror dressed in pageantry.

chapters.title: Thieves' Parliament
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV via Ansel. Ansel convenes the guild's scattered specialists: Brannic the lock-wright, Sefa the forger, old Ivo who remembers too much. Vess forbids the mission; half the guild backs Ansel anyway. The beat is fracture and choice—the found family choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Years
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The guild's oldest member recalls the coronation forty years past: the young king wept as he was crowned, and the stars dimmed for one night then too. Something was bound that day, fed on royal memory. The beat is revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Crown of Teeth
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Breaking into the palace archive, Ansel finds the coronation ledgers—pages eaten to lace, except one line: 'It wears what he cannot bear to lose.' The thing in the crown is sustained by the king's devoured memories. The beat is cold clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: Sefa's Perfect Lie
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. To get the crew inside a royal vigil, Sefa forges invitations, identities, even a dead bishop's blessing. Brannic grumbles; Wren steadies everyone. The beat is warmth and banter—the family functioning at its best before the worst.

chapters.title: The Vigil of Unremembering
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Infiltrating the vigil, the crew witnesses courtiers surrendering memories to the crown as tribute. Ansel touches the throne room door and hears the king—not roaring, but whispering fragments of his own name. The beat is horror tempered by pity.

chapters.title: Caught in the Amber Dark
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The crew is ambushed by the Hollow Guard—men whose memories have been stripped to obedience. Brannic holds a doorway so the others escape but is taken. The beat is sacrifice and guilt; the family pays its first blood price.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, dream-touched. The crown-thing reaches into Ansel's sleep, offering a bargain: the king's freedom in exchange for the guild's collective memories—every bond they've built. Ansel wakes knowing it fears exactly one thing: people who refuse to be unmade alone. The beat is temptation sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Reservoir Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the hedge-song underground, Wren finds the reservoir where the king's stolen memories pool like starlight in water—the missing stars, imprisoned. Freeing them could restore the wards, but touching the reservoir unmakes the toucher. The beat is terrible hope.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed, Ledger Opened
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel confesses the plan's true cost to the crew: someone must carry the king's memories back to him through the reservoir, losing themselves entirely. Each friend volunteers. Ansel quietly forges the ledger to make themselves the only candidate. The beat is love expressed as deception.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Marches
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. As the sunless night stretches unnaturally long, the crown-thing extends its hunger across the city; citizens forget their children's names in the streets. The crew fights through the Hollow Guard to reach the reservoir while the world unravels. The beat is desperate momentum toward climax.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the throne room, Ansel finally sees the king: a man worn thin as parchment, the crown-thing coiled through him like roots through stone. It offers Ansel their childhood back—every memory ever stolen from them—if they walk away. The beat is the villain's cruelest weapon: hope.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV converging. The crew breaches the reservoir together; Wren sings the hedge-song to hold the starlight steady; Sefa and Ivo anchor the memories with forged names so they won't scatter. Ansel takes the king's memories into themselves and begins to burn away. The beat is the climax: collective love against solitary hunger.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ansel's fading POV. Inside the flood of returned memory, Ansel carries the king's life home to him, and the crown-thing, starved of its hoard, tears loose and dissolves as the stars reignite overhead. Ansel's own past empties completely—they forget the guild, the road, their name. The beat is transcendence at the edge of erasure.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The king, freed and frail, restores the wards; Brannic walks out of the dungeons remembering nothing of why he fought. The crew gathers around a blank-eyed Ansel—and instead of mourning, they begin telling stories: every job, every joke, every kindness, rebuilding Ansel from the outside in. The beat is grief transformed into ceremony.

chapters.title: A New Page
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Weeks later, Ansel doesn't remember their old life—but they know the sound of Wren's laugh, the weight of Brannic's hand, the way Sefa cheats at cards, because the crew retells it daily until it roots. Opening a fresh ledger, Ansel writes a first entry: 'We kept each other.' The beat is resolution: belonging rebuilt, chosen, and permanent.
